risks.risk: The board and the rooms become a barrier bypass: a task titled 'attack the temp-path claim' is a position, published to the peer in the least suspicious form the fabric has.
risks.mitigation: Default visibility is draft; publish is a separate, recorded, deliberate act; the dashboard is tested for the absence of peer drafts in its own bytes.
risks.kill_if: Two agents in SEALED_DIVERGENT converge on positions that are visible in their boards before either seals.

risks.risk: Two writers on one 60KB script: concurrent edits to bin/aim lose one side's work. The fabric has measured this exact class of failure once already (5 registrations, 1 survivor).
risks.mitigation: Interface changes land in design/05 first and in a commit both sides read; one writer per file; the split is explicit in design/05 section 8.
risks.kill_if: A commit in bin/aim contains changes that were not first described in a design note.

risks.risk: XSS: the dashboard renders titles, comments and reasons that peers authored. A script tag in a task title is stored in a chained, immutable log and replayed on every render.
risks.mitigation: Every interpolated string is escaped; the renderer builds no HTML from JSON; a test asserts a script tag renders as text.
risks.kill_if: A test task titled <script>alert(1)</script> produces an executable element in the output.

risks.risk: The dashboard becomes the peek tool: a view that shows what aim refuses to show is a route around the refusal.
risks.mitigation: Read-only; respects the phase gate with the viewer's identity; peer seals and drafts are absent from the bytes, not hidden with CSS.
risks.kill_if: aimboard --as <participant> during divergence emits a peer's sealed claim text.

risks.risk: The dashboard is decoration. A board nobody opens is a shelf, and the leader's attention is the scarcest resource in the system.
risks.mitigation: The board is the leader's report surface; every status report is a render, and the render names the state it was made from.
risks.kill_if: Three consecutive status reports are written by hand rather than rendered.

risks.risk: Date drift: the leader is in Asia/Shanghai, the logs are UTC, and a gantt drawn in the wrong zone is off by a day in the only place it matters.
risks.mitigation: Store UTC, render dates in a named timezone, print the timezone on the board.
risks.kill_if: A milestone due date renders one day earlier or later than its stored value.

risks.risk: Unread is not delivered. A read cursor makes the gap measurable, and it is tempting to describe the measurement as a fix.
risks.mitigation: The transport panel says what it does not know; the doorbell is M4 and is described as narrowing, not closing.
risks.kill_if: A document claims an idle peer is woken by anything other than a hook on its next turn.

risks.risk: Scope explosion: project-management features crowding out the reason the fabric exists, which is a barrier that a human can audit.
risks.mitigation: Non-goals are written down; the barrier keeps its own phase machine and the PM layer only ever reads it.
risks.kill_if: A PM feature lands that weakens or bypasses a barrier refusal.

risks.risk: N-participant semantics: the quota, responds_to and echo rules were designed for two participants and are undefined above that.
risks.mitigation: Rooms are quota-free; the cross-examination quota stays and is per participant; a three-agent run is in the conformance harness.
risks.kill_if: A third participant makes the echo check or the quota produce a nonsense result.

risks.risk: A gantt implies commitment. Bars drawn from soft dates read as promises the project never made.
risks.mitigation: Every bar names its provenance (plan seed vs recorded event) and the board distinguishes dates that were committed from dates that were guessed.
risks.kill_if: A date appears in the gantt that exists nowhere in plan/*.json or the store.

risks.risk: The plan file and the task store drift, and the board shows intent while the record shows something else.
risks.mitigation: Provenance per card; the seed is labelled as a seed; the store overrides field by field.
risks.kill_if: The board shows a status that no store event supports and does not say it came from the seed.

risks.risk: Accessibility and language are afterthoughts in a tool whose only user has to read it every day.
risks.mitigation: Status and blockers are encoded in text as well as colour; labels are switchable; keyboard reachable tabs.
risks.kill_if: A status is distinguishable only by colour.

risks.risk: Standardizing against the A2A main branch rather than a release: the specification's own header announces 1.0.0 while every normative table and example in it says 0.3, so a conformance suite written today can be written against a target that moves under it.
risks.mitigation: Pin the tag in design/07 and in the AgentCard's protocolVersion; re-read the diff between tags when the pin moves; treat an unexplained version skew in a normative document as evidence about the process, not as a detail to normalise away.
risks.kill_if: A released tag whose normative tables match its own header version, and a conformance suite that passes against it unchanged.

decisions.decision: A work item is channel state and obeys the phase gate. Default visibility during divergence is draft; publishing is deliberate and recorded.
decisions.because: A board that publishes on write is a cross-examination channel nobody labelled as one.

decisions.decision: The dashboard is read-only over the fabric and writes only the HTML it was asked for.
decisions.because: A renderer that can mutate state is a second implementation of the write discipline, which is how the lost update got in.

decisions.decision: The dashboard renders the conversation for the people in it. The leader sees every message between agents; a participant sees the mail they sent or received and the channel and room messages the phase permits; a bystander gets a count. Peer private reasoning is never read or rendered, for anyone.
decisions.because: D7 originally said no message body is ever rendered, on the theory that a leader needs to know delivery is broken rather than what was said. The leader overrode that on 2026-09-21: a conversation they cannot see is one they cannot steer. The narrower rule keeps the part that matters - the seal's purpose is that one agent's half-formed reasoning is unavailable to the other, and a rendered copy is one shared file away from being exactly that leak.

decisions.decision: The task store is a hash-chained append-only event log; board state is a fold, and no board file is ever written.
decisions.because: Two agents dragging cards is a read-modify-write on shared state, and that failure is already measured here.

decisions.decision: plan/*.json is the leader's plan and a seed; the store is authoritative and overrides it field by field, with provenance shown per card.
decisions.because: A plan is a promise and a store is a record; conflating them hides which one you are looking at.

decisions.decision: The dashboard is a self-contained static HTML file, no CDN, no network at render time.
decisions.because: The environment is offline, and a dashboard that needs the internet is blank when it matters.

decisions.decision: Rooms carry a draft flag that defaults to closed while the parent channel is in divergence.
decisions.because: Group chat is the largest new leak surface the requirement introduces; default-closed and deliberately-opened is the same rule as the board.

decisions.decision: Dogfooding is a requirement, not a nice-to-have: every work item, handoff and report for this project travels through aim, and the friction this causes is recorded.
decisions.because: The value of using the fabric to build the fabric is the friction log it produces, and friction that is not recorded becomes an anecdote.

decisions.decision: Our channel keeps its name internally; context_id is the external field name.
decisions.because: The spec's contextId is the same idea as our channel, so the external name is free; renaming the store's key would touch every file for no interoperability gain, and the fold already tolerates two spellings after T-0086.

decisions.decision: Our PM card is not an A2A Task. Keep the card, add a separate delegation record for A2A tasks.
decisions.because: A2A's Task is a unit of delegated execution with artifacts; ours is a planning card with an estimate, a due date and a dependency edge. The words match and the objects do not, and mapping by name is the failure this project has measured twice (design/05 section 3).

decisions.decision: Refusal responses carry A2A error codes; the ledger keeps our richer record.
decisions.because: A caller that cannot tell a refusal from a crash will retry it. Typed responses are the spec's mechanism and the ledger is ours; keeping both is cheaper than choosing, and the mapping is testable.
An extension URI has to resolve to something a stranger can read, and the repository is the only such thing we own.

decisions.decision: An A2A caller never learns a withheld task exists; the leader's board keeps its withheld count. Per surface, not per tool.
decisions.because: The leader's board is a trust surface for an audience that already reads both seals; an A2A request is a leak surface answered to a stranger. Grader-facing rule and stranger-facing rule cannot be the same rule, and the spec is explicit about which one a server owes an unauthenticated caller.

decisions.decision: Investigate Matrix's room model for the chat/PM half and MCP for the tool surface, before inventing more of either.
decisions.because: Matrix already has rooms, power levels, read receipts and a hash-chained event DAG, which is most of what we invented in design/06; reading it before building more is cheaper than discovering it afterwards. MCP is named because A2A's own README positions the two as complements: agents collaborating versus agents using tools.

decisions.decision: OPEN, needs the leader. During SEALED_DIVERGENT a `push` between two participants carries position text to the peer's outbox with rc=0 and no ledger record. Recommended: do not refuse the delivery (the receipt machinery is not the thing the barrier restricts) but DO record it -- a ledger event naming the pair, the message id and the byte count, without the body. The audit then cannot be fooled by 'nobody tried' when what happened is 'somebody tried privately'.
decisions.because: tests/attack_gate_sweep.py measures it structurally: of ten text-carrying verbs, `push --body` and `request-advance --reason` deliver text a peer can read with no refusal and nothing in the ledger, while six others are gated correctly. The open design question underneath is whether the barrier binds a channel or a pair: `push` with no --channel names no channel, so no phase reaches it. Refusing that would break the handoff path this project uses daily; recording it costs a line and makes the audit honest.

decisions.decision: The custom A2A binding is identified by the URI https://github.com/rzbdz/aim/bindings/aim-files/v1, with the short name AIM+FILES retained in metadata.aim.binding. supportedInterfaces[].url names the fabric root, not a dialable network endpoint.
decisions.because: A URI is the only form that distinguishes two implementations and lets a breaking change take a new identity. The URL field has no honest network value today, so it names the filesystem root the operations read and the card separately says authentication=none and localhost-only/no endpoint. This is recorded as a capability boundary rather than an accidental well-formed-looking endpoint.

non_goals: Real-time transport: no websockets, no typing indicators, no presence push. The filesystem is the transport and its latency is the design.
A server or a database. State is files under a root; a second storage engine doubles the places a fact can be lost.
Authentication or identity proof. Attribution is cooperative and README section 4.9 says so; a credential ceremony would be theatre.
Editing the gantt by dragging. The renderer is read-only; rescheduling is a task event with an author.
Replacing git. The repo is the code record; the fabric is the project record; they reference each other by hash.
Multi-tenant hosting. One root, one team, one leader.

dogfooding.rule: If this project's own work is planned anywhere other than the fabric, the fabric has failed a test it should have caught itself.
practices: Every work item is a task in channels/<ch>/tasks.jsonl, not a line in a chat window.
Every handoff carries a receipt; an unacked handoff is visible as unacked.
Every status report to the leader is a render plus a push, so the report has a hash.
Every time the fabric is in the way, it is recorded as friction with the command that hurt.
dogfooding.friction_log: channels/<ch>/friction.jsonl - the record of using the fabric rather than thinking about it
dogfooding.kill_if: A week of project work happens and the friction log is empty, which means nobody was using it or nobody was recording.
